tldr: Threshold adaptation changes the assignment fiber used by an exact selective randomization test. In the finite fixed-quota design, generic scalar entrances cause strict downward upper-tail jumps; a symbolic paired family gives disconnected valid 95-percent inversion with arbitrarily large independent holdout while the adaptive weight remains positive, specifically \(\lambda=1/(m+1)\). Selector boundaries cap two-tail components at \(2K+1\), and at \(K+1\) when no boundary coincides with a nonpersistent final-score rank equality. The analogous branch cap and simultaneous-event accounting apply to two-stratum select-one/continue-both enrichment; conventional-level sharpness and the primitive branch sign frontier remain open.
gap: Existing selective randomization theory establishes validity and exhibits jagged or disconnected inversion, while fixed-support breakpoint methods locate rank crossings. Neither inspected line of work characterizes p-value jumps from moving conditional fibers together with simultaneous selector/rank endpoints, nor gives the proposed design-level component cap and all-size conventional-level obstruction.
